description: Corpus-wide openCypher-TCK mining coverage, keyed by TCK feature folder (req-gridkin-tck-coverage). Mined against the real openCypher TCK (Apache-2.0), 2026-06-30. CLEAN-ROOM: every intent is in TAP's own words; no TCK query text, graph data, or expected results are copied. `covered` is DERIVED by the guard (count of scenarios whose inspired_by cites the folder); x/y carried-over = covered / (covered + open gaps). `gaps[].kind` records whether a gap is closeable by authoring a test (test), needs a Gryphon language feature first (feature), or is not yet classified (unknown) — refined by probing each gap against the real executor.

gaps.intent: bare unfiltered MATCH (n) all-node scan with no WHERE
gaps.note: every bare_match scenario carries a WHERE; the zero-predicate baseline that would catch an accidental always-on filter is never asserted on the labelless spine

gaps.intent: incoming-direction relationship match (<--)
gaps.note: only --> and undirected are exercised; the direction-inversion executor path is untested

gaps.intent: relationship-type alternation T1|T2 (and redundant T|T collapsing to one)
gaps.note: union-of-types in one hop; separate parse/dispatch path, grammar support unverified

gaps.intent: empty-result relationship match against a non-existent edge
gaps.note: edge files always assume matches exist; the empty-edge-result base case is unexercised

gaps.intent: undirected unanchored match returns BOTH orientations of each edge
gaps.note: our undirected scenarios anchor on an endpoint, so the symmetric double-row behaviour is never asserted

gaps.intent: mixed directed + undirected segments in one pattern
gaps.note: probed 2026-06-30: a multi-hop chain with a directed first hop and an undirected second hop ((a)-[:T]->(b)-[:T]-(c)) routes to the aggregation/advanced executor, which rejects the undirected segment — 'Undirected edge patterns are not supported by the aggregation executor; use -> or <-'. Mixed-direction multi-hop needs engine support

gaps.intent: same variable bound to both relationship endpoints (n)-[r]-(n)
gaps.note: v0 edge scan ignores variable identity (no from==to) — needs engine work

gaps.intent: convergence join: two bound sources onto one target (a)-->(x),(b)-->(x)
gaps.note: intersection/convergence; hub_and_spoke only covers single-source radiation

gaps.intent: disconnected patterns / cross-product across MATCH clauses
gaps.note: cartesian product of independent patterns — easy to get wrong (row explosion), untested

gaps.intent: relationship-uniqueness: reusing one edge variable twice in a pattern is rejected
gaps.note: probed 2026-06-30: the executor does NOT enforce relationship-uniqueness — reusing one edge variable across two hops ((a)-[e:T]->(b)-[e:T]->(c)) executes without error rather than being rejected. Cypher's uniqueness rule needs engine enforcement before a rejection test can assert it

gaps.intent: chained / correlated OPTIONAL MATCH where the second depends on the first's optional var
gaps.note: v0 OPTIONAL MATCH supports exactly one OPTIONAL clause — needs engine work

gaps.intent: multi-hop pattern inside a single OPTIONAL MATCH (all-or-nothing null)
gaps.note: v0 OPTIONAL MATCH requires a single-hop pattern — needs engine work

gaps.intent: optional self-loop match, present vs absent
gaps.note: v0 has no self-loop identity; COUNT(e) counts all out-edges — needs engine work

gaps.intent: projecting optionalVar IS NULL as an open-world matched/unmatched flag
gaps.note: distinguishing matched vs unmatched via IS NULL (not only COUNT)

gaps.intent: null-bound node fed into a later mandatory MATCH yields nothing
gaps.note: v0 allows exactly one mandatory MATCH; multi-MATCH is union not correlation — needs engine work

excluded.intent: variable-length / unbounded relationship paths [*], [*2..n]
excluded.reason: Gryphon has no variable-length traversal

excluded.intent: named paths / path variables p = (...) and length(p)
excluded.reason: no path binding or path functions in Gryphon

excluded.intent: type(r) and other scalar/path functions in RETURN
excluded.reason: Gryphon has no scalar/path function library

excluded.intent: multi-label node conjunction (a:A:B)
excluded.reason: TAP entities carry exactly one entity_type, not a label set

excluded.intent: MERGE-interaction and compile-time variable-type-conflict negatives
excluded.reason: MERGE is a write clause; the type-conflict cases validate constructs Gryphon does not expose

gaps.intent: cross-variable comparison join in WHERE (a.prop = b.prop, a <> b, a.val < b.val)
gaps.note: every predicate compares a property to a literal; comparing two bound variables (equi- and non-equi join) is a core WHERE shape with zero coverage

gaps.intent: multi-variable conjunction constraining two different bound nodes
gaps.note: AND is only ever applied to one variable

gaps.intent: NOT EXISTS over a multi-hop / multi-relationship inner pattern
gaps.note: only single-edge subqueries tested; a longer inner path stresses subquery planning

gaps.intent: pattern-existence predicate mixed into boolean composition (scalar AND existence)
gaps.note: combining NOT EXISTS as one branch of AND/OR rather than a standalone filter

excluded.intent: affirmative EXISTS { pattern } and full existential subquery with RETURN/WITH/aggregation/nesting
excluded.reason: Gryphon's existence form is the NOT EXISTS negated pattern predicate only

excluded.intent: existential subquery containing a write/update clause must fail
excluded.reason: Gryphon is read-only; the clause cannot appear

excluded.intent: path-length predicates length(p) in WHERE
excluded.reason: depends on path variables, which Gryphon lacks

gaps.intent: default-ascending order when the ASC/DESC token is omitted
gaps.note: our asc scenarios state asc explicitly; the implicit-default path is unwitnessed

gaps.intent: ORDER BY a RETURN alias whose sort priority differs from projection order
gaps.note: we order by aggregated columns but never a plain projected alias with divergent priority

gaps.intent: constant expression in ORDER BY is inert (no influence on order)
gaps.note: cheap determinism pin, untested

gaps.intent: ORDER BY an undefined / unknown key fails
gaps.note: no negative scenario for sorting on an unknown variable

gaps.intent: aggregation-misuse in ORDER BY fails (bare aggregate / sort on DISTINCT-removed var)
gaps.note: error paths untested

excluded.intent: temporal-type ordering (date/time/datetime property types)
excluded.reason: not part of the Gryphon/TAP data-lane surface; the asc/desc + NULL-placement mechanics are already covered via int/string scans

excluded.intent: DISTINCT-dependent ordering corners
excluded.reason: contingent on DISTINCT semantics — a separate coverage axis, not ORDER BY

excluded.intent: all SKIP scenarios and SKIP+LIMIT combinations
excluded.reason: Gryphon has no SKIP clause (LIMIT-only)

gaps.intent: UNION deduplication actually triggered — an element present in BOTH arms collapses to one
gaps.note: our two union arms are disjoint types (pg_hub vs pg_node), so the defining dedup semantic of distinct union is never exercised

excluded.intent: UNION ALL and mixed UNION / UNION ALL
excluded.reason: Gryphon performs only deduplicated union

excluded.intent: scalar/literal-row union (RETURN 1 UNION RETURN 2) and column-compatibility validation
excluded.reason: Gryphon union is a graph-envelope merge of MATCH clauses, not column-aligned scalar-row union

gaps.intent: COUNT(expr) skips null/absent values while still counting the row's group
gaps.note: probed 2026-06-30: node-only property grouping (MATCH (n:pg_node) RETURN n.data.kind, COUNT(...)) is rejected by the executor — 'Advanced executor requires at least one edge in the MATCH pattern'. COUNT-with-grouping is only reachable through a relationship pattern, so the null-skipping COUNT(expr) semantic needs an engine path for edgeless grouping before a test can assert it

gaps.intent: COUNT of a self-loop / degenerate self-referential edge
gaps.note: edge-counting around self-loops is an easy off-by-one source

excluded.intent: non-COUNT aggregates (min/max/sum/avg/collect/percentile/stdev)
excluded.reason: Gryphon's only aggregate is COUNT

excluded.intent: COUNT DISTINCT / collect(DISTINCT ...)
excluded.reason: Gryphon's COUNT exposes no DISTINCT modifier

gaps.intent: disjunction across relationship-type predicates (type=X OR type=Y)
gaps.note: OR is only tested over node-property / IN comparisons

excluded.intent: XOR exclusive disjunction and its algebra
excluded.reason: XOR is not in Gryphon's grammar (AND/OR/NOT only)

excluded.intent: null-operand boolean truth tables and null-propagation through AND/OR
excluded.reason: Cypher three-valued quirks; Gryphon uses two-valued IS KNOWN/IS UNKNOWN

excluded.intent: fail-on-non-boolean operand to AND/OR/NOT
excluded.reason: Gryphon's grammar only admits boolean predicates as operands

gaps.intent: unobserved/null LHS IN a list -> non-member (false), not null
gaps.note: no scenario feeds a null LHS into IN

excluded.intent: list subscripting / slicing, list-typed LHS, nested-list membership
excluded.reason: Gryphon has no indexing/slice operators; membership is scalar-against-list only

excluded.intent: list equality, concatenation, range(), comprehension, reverse, head/tail/last, size()
excluded.reason: none of these list constructors/operations exist in Gryphon's read-only grammar

gaps.intent: JSON key-path access is case-sensitive (data.tags.Team vs data.tags.team)
gaps.note: JSON-path backends can silently fold/mismatch; no scenario pins exact-case lookup

gaps.intent: distinguish an absent key from a key present with an explicit null value, in a predicate
gaps.note: our absent-key scenario conflates the two; the missing-vs-explicit-null distinction is a live grid convention

gaps.intent: sub-key access walking into a non-map scalar (data.tags is a string, then .team)
gaps.note: behaviour walking a key path into a non-object value is undefined (null vs error)

excluded.intent: dynamic bracket map access map[$expr] with parameters and its type errors
excluded.reason: Gryphon predicates use static dotted JSON paths, no parameters or runtime bracket indexing

excluded.intent: keys() builtin and key-existence via 'x' IN keys(map)
excluded.reason: Gryphon exposes no keys() function

excluded.intent: map-literal construction / projection
excluded.reason: out of Gryphon's read-only data-access scope

gaps.intent: keyword case-insensitivity of IS NULL / IS NOT NULL (and IS KNOWN / IS UNKNOWN)
gaps.note: no scenario pins the parser's case folding; a regression to case-sensitive keywords would go uncaught

gaps.intent: IS NULL / IS UNKNOWN on a property of a node that itself was never bound (unmatched optional row)
gaps.note: our null files only exercise a present node with a missing property, not the null-node path

excluded.intent: null = null / null <> null evaluating to null, and NOT null = null
excluded.reason: three-valued-logic equality; Gryphon is two-valued (null = unobserved)

excluded.intent: literal null IS NULL in a bare RETURN, and IS NULL on a map-literal key via WITH
excluded.reason: Gryphon evaluates IS KNOWN/IS UNKNOWN against matched fields, not free literals; no map literals or WITH

gaps.intent: NOT-negated string predicate (NOT name STARTS_WITH 'ab')
gaps.note: string_match has zero NOT coverage

gaps.intent: whitespace needle matched literally (no implicit trimming)
gaps.note: leading/trailing space in the needle is significant

gaps.intent: newline/tab control-char needle matched literally (no normalization)
gaps.note: embedded control chars treated as literal

gaps.intent: exact full-value match (needle equals the entire value)
gaps.note: our scenarios only exercise strict sub-portions

gaps.intent: multi-predicate AND combinations (prefix AND suffix; prefix AND substring AND suffix)
gaps.note: conjunctive narrowing on one field, untested

excluded.intent: scalar string functions: substring, trim, reverse, split, toUpper/toLower, concat, length, replace, regex-replace
excluded.reason: Gryphon is read-only with no scalar string functions

no_applicable_folder.reason: openCypher TCK has no regex coverage — the String13/String14 feature files are empty stubs and the =~ operator appears in zero TCK feature files. regex_match corner cases are self-authored, not TCK-mined.
TAP-native: Entity dimension scoping has no openCypher analog.
TAP-native: post-upsert write-path read of USES_PANEL edges; TCK is read-only MATCH.
